title: Shared stable Koopman operator with sparse private nonlinear residuals
hypothesis: A shared low-rank regime-conditioned linear latent operator plus a sparse private nonlinear residual for exceptional regimes preserves long-horizon quality with fewer complete bytes than independent nonlinear dynamics, while shared-only errors localize where private capacity is needed.

development.tuning: none; least-squares operator and residual fit

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed after exact native shared/private alias or a quality/storage/stability gate miss.

controls: independent full linear operator and private nonlinear residual per regime
shared operator codes without nonlinear residual
Mirror shared operator plus sparse private nonlinear correction
native conditional low-rank operator plus the same sparse private correction
metrics: shared-only error on exceptional vs common regimes

paid: private residual basis and active indices/values

pass_gate: Horizon-40 nRMSE <=0.02, max local Jacobian spectral radius <1, at least 25% fewer bytes than independent, private corrections active only where needed, and strict improvement over native shared/private controls.
fail_gate: FAIL Mirror-specific value on exact native control alias, quality/stability miss, insufficient savings, or no native-control frontier improvement.

compute.active_MACs: direct operator-factor applications + shared forcing map + nonlinear feature and output correction
compute.wall_time: small CPU rollout calibration, not throughput evidence

boundaries: Synthetic known feature residual and linear latent operator only; no learned Deep Koopman or nonlinear discovery claim.
Residual feature direction w and residual output basis are fitted from development trajectories; only active regime scalars are stored privately.
Test trajectories are independent of development sequences but use the same registered regimes.
Native low-rank operator plus private scalar nonlinear residual is a mandatory direct control.
